subject: Scheduling Dedicated Capacity Sizing Call
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up & next steps from today's discovery call

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the call this morning - really appreciate the context on FintechCo's roadmap and where you're prioritizing signed-in user experiences. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal: Understand Dedicated capacity needs (throughput, latency SLOs, peak concurrency) and map to a capacity sizing proposal and rough cost estimate.
- Action: Schedule a 60-min capacity sizing call / technical deep dive with your infra/ML engineering and our runtime team.

I've attached a lightweight capacity template (capacity_template.xlsx) that helps capture: average qps, peak qps, average request length (tokens), typical prompt/response token distribution, KV cache hit expectations, and target p99/p50 latency SLOs. If you can drop that in ahead of the call it'll let us prepare concrete sizing and model variant recommendations.

Proposed times (all PT):
- Wed 17 Feb, 9:00:00am
- Wed 17 Feb, 2:00:00pm
- Thu 18 Feb, 11:00:00pm

If none of those work, share 2 slots that do and I'll send a calendar invite. I've also included a Calendly link below if easier.

Attachments: capacity_template.xlsx (Excel)
Related link: https://calendly.com/redwood/30min

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0182

From: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from today's discovery call

Marissa - thanks for the recap and the template. This is helpful.

We can do Wed 17 Feb 2pm PT. I'll loop in our ML infra lead and one backend infra owner - cc'ed below. A couple of clarifying points so your team can prep:

- Expected steady-state throughput: ~120 requests/sec across 60 app servers.
- Estimated peak (flash sale / marketing): up to 1,200 requests/sec for ~5-10 minutes.
- Typical request size: 40 tokens in, 300 tokens out (few-shot prompts).
- Target latency SLO: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 700ms for the 95% of traffic that is interactive; background batch jobs can be relaxed.

I'm adding our ML infra lead, Camila Reyes (camila.reyes@fintechco.com), and our backend owner, David Kim (david.kim@fintechco.com), to coordinate. We'll aim to populate the template before the meeting but want to confirm the 2pm slot.

Thanks,
Jordan
VP Infrastructure | FintechCo

Thanks Jordan - 2pm PT on Wed 17th works for our team. I'm Camila from Redwood's runtime/product; I'll lead the capacity sizing and kernel selection discussion. A couple requests so we can come prepared: 

- If you can paste a short sample of request/response payloads (sanitized) into the template or share a small log extract, that helps us estimate tokenization and KV cache behavior.
- Confirm whether you prioritize consistent p99 latency across interactive traffic, or prefer prioritized tail latency for a subset of requests (we can recommend different sharding/burst policies).
- Any data residency or private deployment constraints (VPC, on-prem)?

I'm attaching our SLO checklist (slo_requirements.pdf) that outlines the inputs we use to size dedicated pools and estimate GPU types/quantization.

We'll treat the first 20-30 minutes as discovery to validate numbers, then walk through a capacity map and recommended configs.

Attachments: slo_requirements.pdf (PDF)


Camila Reyes
